summary: Narrows lookout in Chattooga County: a 42-foot steel tower built by the CCC in 1941 and dismantled in 1978, per a district history quoted by Eastern US Forest Lookouts.

facts.design: Steel structure, 42 feet tall, with a 12-by-12-foot wooden cab and a four-foot catwalk with guardrails
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1978 per the Armuchee Ranger District history quoted by Eastern US Forest Lookouts. No source describes the site now.

events.note: Constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps

evidence.supports: built 1941 by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: This steel structure was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1941.

evidence.supports: 42 feet tall with a 12 by 12 foot wooden cab
evidence.quote: The tower was 42 feet in height with a 12 foot by 12 foot wooden cab.

evidence.supports: four-foot catwalk with guardrails around the cab
evidence.quote: A four foot wide catwalk with guardrails encircled the exterior of the cab.

evidence.supports: filed under Chattahoochee National Forest, Chattooga County
evidence.quote: Georgia - Chattooga County - Chattahoochee National Forest

corrections.why: The cited page gives the tower as 42 feet in height, which is 12.8 m. The 3.7 m figure is about 12 feet, the width of the wooden cab, so it looks like a cab dimension was recorded as height.

notes_for_editor: Single historical source: the Eastern US Forest Lookouts page quotes a history of the Armuchee Ranger District (not located). Two web searches found nothing about this tower beyond the list entry. Coordinates and elevation come only from the TN Landforms table. Do not confuse with Narrows, Georgia (Banks County), a different place. Lead: Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest heritage staff, or the district history the Eastern US page quotes. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Armuchee Ranger District attribution is confirmed on the Eastern US page, and all dates and dimensions match its quotes. Elevation units: the TN Landforms list does not label them; 1,657 is read as feet, because the same list gives Brasstown Lookout Tower as 4,735 and Brasstown Bald, Georgia's highest point, is about 4,784 feet, so the figure cannot be metres.
